water.title: Jewish Water Rituals - Returning to the Flow of Creation
water.aboutBody: The Jewish Water Rituals at Casa Romero invite participants to enter the sacred element of water as a living teacher. Rooted in the ancient tradition of mikvah and renewed through contemporary ecological awareness, these ceremonies are held outdoors at the river and natural springs on our property. Each immersion is guided by intention, preparation, and prayer—an embodied process of release and return.
water.riverBody: The waters that feed Casa Romero come from mountain springs known locally as quebradas—streams that have sustained human and more-than-human life for millennia. Immersions here are not symbolic; they are ecological acts of reciprocity. Each participant is invited to listen to the river's rhythms, to offer gratitude, and to leave no trace beyond prayer and breath.
water.decolonizingBody: Our approach reconnects the practice of immersion to the earth that sustains it. In many communities, water ritual has been separated from the land, confined to tiled pools and private walls. Here, the mountain streams of Boyacá become the vessel—reclaiming immersion as a dialogue with creation.
water.expectBody: Participants begin with quiet reflection and intention-setting guided by a facilitator. The ritual may include song, spoken prayer, or silence depending on the needs of each person. Immersions are gender-inclusive and body-positive, grounded in consent, safety, and care.
water.bookBody: Individual and small-group immersions can be arranged year-round, weather permitting. Ceremonies are tailored for life transitions, healing journeys, or moments of spiritual renewal.
retreats.title: Solo Retreats - Time for Stillness and Reconnection
retreats.amenitiesList: Private cabin, casita, or yurt with mountain or garden view
Outdoor spaces for meditation, writing, and art
Shared kitchen and library with books on ecology and ritual
River trail access for bathing and reflection
Optional herbal steam or sweat-lodge experience
retreats.dailyBody: Days unfold without clocks or noise. Mornings often begin with tea at sunrise, followed by writing, prayer, or walking meditation. Afternoons invite rest, journaling, or exploring the forest paths. Evenings bring simple shared meals or quiet stargazing over the valley.
retreats.bookBody: Retreats may be scheduled for a few days or several weeks.
immersion.title: Spanish Immersion - Learn Through Land and Community
immersion.focusBody: The immersion is designed for all levels. Instruction integrates conversation, art, song, and ecological vocabulary so students learn to think in Spanish as they move through lived experience. Mornings may include guided study; afternoons are spent practicing with community members in the gardens or kitchen. The goal is fluency of relationship, not perfection of grammar.
immersion.includedList: Daily language sessions with native teachers
Farm-to-table meals and shared cooking practice
Art and movement workshops for experiential learning
Community conversation circles and field excursions
Simple lodging and access to the surrounding trails
immersion.overviewBody: Our Spanish Immersion program is not a classroom. It is an embodied, relational way of learning that happens through everyday life on the land: cooking, gardening, storytelling, and shared laughter. Participants practice the language of daily care—how to ask for what the soil needs, how to tell stories around the fire, how to listen to the wind.
immersion.stayBody: Guests stay in rustic, comfortable rooms built with local materials. Wi-Fi is limited by design to encourage presence and slow living. Meals are shared family-style, emphasizing local produce and traditional preparation methods.
immersion.bookBody: Sessions are available year-round with flexible durations.
about.title: Casa Romero — A Decolonization Retreat Center in Boyacá, Colombia
about.heroAlt: Mountain valley landscape near Boyacá, Colombia
about.purposeBody: Casa Romero is a living experiment in remembering how to live well with the land. Rooted in Indigenous and Jewish ecological wisdom, it offers a space to unlearn the patterns of colonization through language, ritual, and relationship. The retreat center welcomes all who wish to reconnect with the earth and participate in healing the stories that separate people from place.
about.purposeImgAlt: Hillside with trees around Casa Romero
about.whereBody: Nestled in the highlands of Boyacá, Colombia, Casa Romero sits on sacred Muisca territory surrounded by mountains, waterfalls, and rich soils. The property includes gardens, forested hillsides, and a freshwater spring, offering visitors a direct encounter with the vitality of the land. Our architecture blends traditional clay and bamboo with modern sustainability practices, keeping the footprint light and the air clean.
about.whereImgAlt: Forest creek and rocks near the retreat grounds
about.missionBody1: Our mission is to support personal and collective decolonization through immersive, land-based experiences that weave together cultural memory, traditional medicine, and spiritual practice.
about.missionBody2: We envision a world in which every person remembers their belonging to the earth, speaks from ancestral integrity, and contributes to a network of communities grounded in reciprocity and care.
about.approachBody: Everything that happens here—language immersion, ritual practice, herbal study, or solitude—is guided by the rhythm of the land. Days begin with quiet time for prayer or reflection, followed by work in the gardens, river walks, or study under the trees. Guests participate not as tourists but as temporary community members contributing to an ecosystem of learning.
about.offeringsSpanishDesc: — learn language through relationship, art, and ecology.
about.offeringsSoloDesc: — restorative time for quiet, reflection, and reconnection with nature.
about.offeringsWaterDesc: — ritual practice at the confluence of tradition and landscape.
about.whyBody: Colombia is a place of extraordinary biodiversity and cultural renewal. For generations, the region's Indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities have preserved knowledge about balance and regeneration. By situating Casa Romero here, we honor those lineages and invite international visitors to engage with the heart of decolonization work in a living landscape of resistance and rebirth.
